A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ForageWorld study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated future-work and licensing sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent-training experiments, behavioral analyses, architecture ablations and recurrent-state decoding results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds single-neuron encoding analyses, PQN experiments and expanded front-facing-vision results.

M1.justification: The PPO-GRU architecture, reward, auxiliary position loss and pruning procedure remain unchanged. Appendix D extends the analysis toolkit with GLMs predicting individual-neuron activity from binned position, supplementing the existing position decoders and patch-choice GLM.

E1.justification: The experiments retain ForageWorld and its existing arena, sensory and predator scenarios. PQN and the neuron analyses use this same environment. Curriculum learning, LLM agents and multi-agent environments are discussed only as future directions.

E2.justification: v1 compares PPO-based architecture and objective variants. v2 adds the distinct off-policy PQN-LSTM comparator against PPO-GRU, with performance, trajectory and behavioral comparisons in Appendix E and Figures 29–31.

E3.justification: The new neuron analysis uses 14×14 position bins, normalized neural activity and a 70/30 within-episode training/test split. PQN introduces exploration schedules and a 12-billion-timestep budget, versus the retained 3-billion-timestep PPO setup. These are additional protocols; the existing ridge-decoding 75/25 split remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds substantial analyses of single-neuron spatial tuning, training/test fit agreement and radial encoding across PPO with and without the auxiliary loss and PQN. Appendix E examines exploration failures and contrasting predator strategies. Figure 15 also expands the existing front-facing-vision learning-history analysis.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the uncertainty displays in Figures 3 and 4 as 95% confidence intervals and states a default confidence-interval convention in the checklist. Figure 2 retains five seeds and standard-deviation shading; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: New results include approximately 100/512 position-sensitive neurons and increasing radial responses even without the auxiliary loss. Appendix E reports that only 30% of PQN runs in the two successful configurations performed comparably to PPO, with less predator killing under different training settings. Figure 15 updates and extends the plotted history; Figure 9 corrects the reported entropy trends without changing its curves.

T1.justification: The reward, auxiliary-loss, PPO and ridge-regression equations are retained. Neither version presents theoretical results or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive formal assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introductory contributions retain their substantive claims: ForageWorld, a reusable behavioral-neural toolkit, emergent planning-like behavior in model-free RNNs and a reproducible code pipeline. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a distance-accumulation explanation for origin revisitation and attributes PQN failures to inadequate exploration, while contrasting PPO fighting with PQN evasion. Figure 9 now explains the late entropy increase through the training objective. These additions are not fully reconciled with retained statements about PPO primarily evading predators and auxiliary-loss removal eliminating spatial representations.

D1.justification: Table 3 adds PQN hyperparameters and search ranges; Appendix D documents NeMoS fitting, neural normalization, spatial binning and clustering. Figure 4 newly specifies the 1500-step early/late boundary and 250-step angular-variance window. Section 3 replaces the anonymous code address with an identified GitHub repository.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and targeted discussion concerning foraging beyond bandit tasks, interpretable RL, emergent planning, PQN, NeMoS and future navigation architectures. The central positioning as a behavior-first bridge between RL and neuroscience remains intact.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section organization remain intact, with localized clarifications and caption revisions. The curriculum discussion moves to Appendix A.7 and expands; new appendices and a conference checklist are added, and acknowledgments are expanded. This is not a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 19–31, expands Table 3, redraws Figure 15 and corrects Figure 9's heading. Several existing appendix figures are regrouped, and a compact author block allows the complete abstract onto the first page. The graphics in Figures 1–5 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendices D–E broaden the empirical support beyond v1's PPO-focused analyses and disclose PQN failures. Corrected entropy reporting and additional protocol and uncertainty details improve clarity and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by differing PPO/PQN architectures and budgets, and incomplete reconciliation of the new spatial-encoding and predator-strategy findings with retained interpretations.
